Error.description:

message, and, where they apply, the feature, the elements at fault (the first of them, and
how many in all), the request's field at fault, the cause, what to do, and the names that

`change_the_values` (the request's values crashed the worker, and would again: change

operation, or try again), `try_again` (it wasn't the values: try the request again),
or `try_once_more` (only once more: the worker may have been stopped for the memory
the request used). Null for any other error, and a fault whose advice is in its
suggestion's words alone.

elements_total.description: How many elements are at fault, listed or not.

feature.description: The ID of the feature at fault, if one is.

message.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

Limits.description:

use. A request past one is refused, as `invalid_input`, unless its description says
otherwise.

disk_check_ms.description:

on disk to the start of the next: not refused. Only `status` starts one, when none is
running and the last ended at least this long ago, so `status`'s `disk`, a

drag_move_seconds.description:

stopped, a `worker_timeout`, and the drag ends. A drag's whole solves (its begin's,
its end's) take a sketch's solve's time.

kernel_seconds.description:

listed.description:
How many errors (or problems, or warnings) a response lists: the rest are counted,
never refused.

log_bytes.description:
The most text a session's log buffer keeps, in bytes, counted as a read counts it:
not refused, the oldest events are dropped and counted.

log_events.description:

and counted (`read_logs`' `dropped`).

log_read_bytes.description:

features): a read stops before the event that would pass it, its `next` saying where.

published_reads.description: How many reads of the published model run at once in one session.

query.description: The most entries a `query` returns: its `limit` at most.

query_measures.description: The most ranges a `query`'s `measures` holds: one a measure.

render_seconds.description:

render_side.description: The most pixels a `render`'s image is across or high.

sessions.description: How many sessions one process holds open at once.

sketch_seconds.description: How long one sketch's solve may take, in seconds: past it, a `worker_timeout`.

undo_bytes.description:

Angle.description: An angle in degrees: a number, to at most 9 decimals (nanodegrees). An exponent is read exactly; Silico writes plain decimals. (Strings are reserved for expressions, which aren't read yet.)

Axis.description: What a revolve or groove turns about: x_axis (the sketch's, from its origin along +x), y_axis (along +y), or the ID of a line of the sketch, construction or not, from its `from` point to its `to`.

AxisToken.description: A global axis, signed, as a sketch on a face names its x.

ChamferSize.description:
How far a chamfer cuts each edge back: along both its faces alike. (The uneven forms,
measured from one of each edge's faces, are left for later: which face is the document's
to name, not OCCT's order to pick.)

Coordinate.description: A value the solver works out, in millimetres: a number, read correctly rounded to the nearest 64-bit float, and written in full as the shortest decimal that reads back as it. Within a kilometre of the origin.

Direction.description:
How two curves meeting at a point run there: on in the `same` direction (a smooth
join), or back the `opposite` way (a cusp).

ElementId.description: A sketch element's ID: 8 characters of Crockford's base32 in lower case (digits and letters but i, l, o, and u), unique within its sketch.

ElementName.description: An element of an earlier feature's solid, by its name in Silico's form (feature.type.Kind(...)), never by its number. A sketch's elements appear only as sources in what a feature made of them, by ID (sketch.sketch.Edge.<id>, sketch.sketch.Vertex.<id>), its only region sketch.sketch.Face1: a pad's side face is pad.pad.Face(G sketch.sketch.Edge.<id>).

FacePlane.description:
A sketch on a planar face (docs/ports/attacher.md, *What Silico does*): the face, by its
name in Silico's form, found in the solids live at the sketch's place at each rebuild;
the global axis the sketch's x follows, projected onto the face; and whether the sketch
is flipped, its normal and x negated and its y kept. Where it then sits is the
rebuild's to say: nothing of the frame is stored.

face.description:
The face, by its name, as Silico names it (`k7f2qx3m.box.Face6`), of a feature
before the sketch.

reversed.description:
Whether the sketch is flipped: its normal into the face's solid, not out of it, and
its x against the axis's projection; its y kept.

x.description: The global axis the sketch's x follows: projected onto the face, it's the sketch's x.

FeatureId.description: A feature's ID: 8 characters of Crockford's base32 in lower case (digits and letters but i, l, o, and u).

FeatureVersion.description: The feature's version: changing a feature type's behaviour bumps it, and a document keeps the behaviour it was made with. 1 for every type so far.

Length.description: A length in millimetres: a number, to at most 6 decimals (nanometres). An exponent is read exactly; Silico writes plain decimals. (Strings are reserved for expressions, which aren't read yet.)

LineSide.description:
Which side of a line, facing from its start (`from`) to its end (`to`); for an axis,
facing along it (+x, +y).

Name.description: A display name, which needn't be unique.

NewFeature.description: A feature as the document writes it, to add to the timeline. Its id may be left out, for one the core makes that no feature holds, and its v, for the type's current version. A fingerprint is refused, but for null: a commit writes it. Each member the feature may leave out (its id, v, note, and fingerprint, and a pad's or revolve's base) may be given as null, which is the same as leaving it out.

`height` along z.
A cylinder along z, its base centred on `position`.
A sphere centred on `position`.

A cone along z, its base (`radius1`) centred on `position`, `radius2` at `height`.
Either radius may be zero, not both.

A torus around z, centred on `position`: `radius1` from the axis to the tube's
centre, `radius2` the tube's.
Everything in either of two features' solids.
`base`'s solid less what's in `tool`'s.
What's in both of two features' solids.
A constrained 2D sketch (docs/design/m3.2-sketch-format.md).

point.

note.description: A note about the feature, kept with it (left out when there's none). Null is the same as left out.

isn't suppressed leaves it out).

One of the origin's planes, oriented as FreeCAD's (D6). On `xy`, the sketch's x is +X
and its y +Y (normal +Z); on `xz`, x is +X and y +Z (normal −Y); on `yz`, x is +Y and
y +Z (normal +X).

Lengths are above 0; `reversed` only where it changes the solid.

of the model, by its name, with the axis the sketch's x follows and whether it's flipped
(docs/ports/attacher.md, F1 and F2; M5.9).

How far a pocket goes from its sketch's plane: a pad's forms, or through everything of
its base along its direction (against it when `reversed`).

`length / 2` each way from the plane.
`length` along the feature's direction and `length2` against it.

Through everything of its base along the feature's direction, or against it when
`reversed`.

SketchArc.description:
An arc about `center`, counter-clockwise from `start` to `end`. Its points are its
definition: its radius and angles are the solver's, worked out from them, and the
solve holds its ends on it (D2, arcs).

radius.description: Worked out by the solver, as coordinates are.

SketchConstraint.description: One constraint: its ID and its form.

The two points level.
One point above the other.
The line's length.
The distance between two points.
x(b) − x(a), signed.
y(b) − y(a), signed.
The point's distance from the line (extended), on the given side of it.
The point on the curve: a line extended, or an arc's whole circle, as FreeCAD's.

`b`'s direction taken from its `to` to its `from`, so the angle is to the ray
that leaves a corner `b` ends at (written only as true; an angle measured to `b`

A circle's or arc's diameter.
Two lines of equal length, or two circles or arcs of equal radius.
Tangent along their edges: a line and a circle or arc, or two circles or arcs.

SketchPoint.description: A point of the sketch, which curves share.

tools.description: Suppress one feature (`suppressed: true`) or unsuppress it (`false`). A suppressed feature isn't built: a feature that consumes it builds on the nearest unsuppressed feature up its chain, so suppressing a part's first hole leaves the part. Edit inside a transaction: `begin`, the edits, then `commit` to save them or `rollback` to undo them all. An edit made outside one is saved to the file at once, with no undo but another edit. After an edit, read with `model: "current"`, which waits for the edit's rebuild; `published` answers at once from the newest model rebuilt, which may be older.

tools.description: Add points, lines, circles, arcs, and constraints to one sketch, each as the document writes it with a fresh random 8-character ID, never one the sketch holds or a removal freed (a name a feature stores of the removed member would find the new one); a new curve may end at a point the sketch holds, joining it there. tools.description: Join the two pieces a split left at a point into one curve again, split's inverse: two lines held on one line by a `tangent_at` (`same`) at the point, or two arcs about one centre (a split circle's two arcs make its circle again). The piece that ends there keeps its ID and takes the other's far end (it's the one curve in `modified`, the other piece in `removed`); the other piece, the point, and the constraints naming the point go, and constraints on the other piece move to the kept one. An edit made outside one is saved to the file at once, with no undo but another edit. After an edit, read with `model: "current"`, which waits for the edit's rebuild; `published` answers at once from the newest model rebuilt, which may be older.
